description: Project Euler 1 through 255 in C and Rust, through 120 in Gforth, and 191 selected native Factor implementations (71 in the 121–255 extension). Answers are exact output strings, including decimals, hexadecimal, fractions, and coordinate lists.

problems.title: Lattice Paths
problems.method: One-row dynamic programming sums paths arriving from above and the left.

problems.title: Maximum Path Sum I
problems.method: Bottom-up dynamic programming on the official fifteen-row triangle.

problems.title: Non-Abundant Sums
problems.method: Divisor sieve and abundant pair sums through the statement's sufficient bound 28123.

problems.title: Lexicographic Permutations
problems.method: Factorial-block unranking of zero-based permutation index 999999.

problems.title: Reciprocal Cycles
problems.method: Long division detects the first repeated remainder for every denominator below 1000.

problems.title: Coin Sums
problems.method: Coin-by-coin dynamic programming counts unordered representations of 200 pence.

problems.title: Pandigital Products
problems.method: Exhaust the possible one-by-four and two-by-three digit products; deduplicate products.

problems.title: Digit Cancelling Fractions
problems.method: Exhaust proper two-digit fractions, cancel equal nonzero digits, and check exact cross products.

problems.title: Double-base Palindromes
problems.method: Check ordinary decimal and binary digit reversal for each odd integer below one million.

problems.title: Truncatable Primes
problems.method: Traverse the entire right-truncatable-prime tree, testing each node's left truncations.

problems.title: Pandigital Multiples
problems.method: Enumerate starting integers below 10000 and concatenate successive multiples until nine digits.

problems.title: Pandigital Prime
problems.method: Descending digit permutations, omitting digit lengths divisible by three in digit sum.

problems.title: Coded Triangle Numbers
problems.method: Parse the 1786 official words; test whether eight times each score plus one is an exact square.

problems.title: Sub-string Divisibility
problems.method: Permutation backtracking prunes each three-digit divisibility constraint as soon as it is known.

problems.title: Triangular, Pentagonal, and Hexagonal
problems.method: Enumerate hexagonal numbers above 40755 and use the exact pentagonal discriminant test.

problems.title: Prime Permutations
problems.method: Exhaust four-digit prime arithmetic progressions and compare digit-count signatures.

problems.title: Prime Digit Replacements
problems.method: Sieve by increasing digit length; enumerate all same-digit position masks and ten replacements.

problems.title: Permuted Multiples
problems.method: Search increasing decimal ranges and compare exact digit multiplicities of n through 6n.

problems.title: Combinatoric Selections
problems.method: Pascal recurrence saturates at 1000001, preserving the threshold without large integers.

problems.title: Poker Hands
problems.method: Pack hand category and complete tie breakers into a base-15 integer; includes five-high ace straights.

problems.title: Powerful Digit Sum
problems.method: Exact GMP powers for all positive a,b below 100, followed by decimal digit sums.

problems.title: Square Root Convergents
problems.method: Exact GMP recurrence p/q -> (p+2q)/(p+q), comparing actual decimal string lengths.

problems.title: Spiral Primes
problems.method: Test the three nonsquare corners of each layer; compare the prime ratio with exact integers.

problems.title: XOR Decryption
problems.method: Exhaust all 26^3 lowercase keys; use a documented English-frequency and common-word score. This identification is heuristic; the selected official plaintext and ASCII sum are checked.

problems.title: Prime Pair Sets
problems.method: Minimum five-clique search in the concatenation-prime graph. Discover a finite upper bound, then exhaust every prime below that sum to establish minimality.

problems.title: Cyclical Figurate Numbers
problems.method: Backtrack through four-digit polygonal numbers using two-digit overlaps, one type and one value each.

problems.title: Cubic Permutations
problems.method: Group complete digit-length buckets of cubes by digit counts, then select groups of exactly five.

problems.title: Powerful Digit Counts
problems.method: Compare exact powers of bases 1 through 9 against successive decimal lower bounds.

problems.title: Odd Period Square Roots
problems.method: Count odd continued-fraction periods using the integer square-root recurrence.

problems.title: Convergents of e
problems.method: Generate 100 convergent numerators with GMP and sum the final decimal digits.

problems.title: Diophantine Equation
problems.method: Find fundamental Pell solutions among continued-fraction convergents and compare their exact GMP numerators.

problems.title: Maximum Path Sum II
problems.method: Bottom-up dynamic programming over the official 100-row triangle.

problems.title: Magic 5-gon Ring
problems.method: Enumerate inner nodes, derive outer nodes from a common sum, canonicalize rotation and maximize the 16-digit string.

problems.title: Totient Permutation
problems.method: Sieve every totient below ten million and compare permutation candidates by exact cross products.

problems.title: Ordered Fractions
problems.method: Enumerate denominators and their largest reduced numerator strictly below 3/7.

problems.title: Counting Fractions
problems.method: Sum the totient sieve for denominators 2 through one million.

problems.title: Counting Fractions in a Range
problems.method: Count the mediant tree between Farey neighbours 1/3 and 1/2, pruning by denominator.

problems.title: Digit Factorial Chains
problems.method: Memoize distinct chain lengths, separating newly discovered cycles from prefixes and cached tails.

problems.title: Singular Integer Right Triangles
problems.method: Generate primitive Euclidean triples and count perimeter multiples, saturating at two.

problems.title: Counting Summations
problems.method: Use unordered coin-change partitions with allowed parts 1 through 99.

problems.title: Prime Summations
problems.method: Use prime coin-change partitions with an expanding bound and threshold-saturated counts.

problems.title: Coin Partitions
problems.method: Evaluate the generalized pentagonal recurrence modulo one million until a zero residue.

problems.title: Passcode Derivation
problems.method: Topologically order all observed digits; the acyclic one-occurrence ordering attains the minimum possible length.

problems.title: Square Root Digital Expansion
problems.method: Compute exact scaled integer square roots with GMP and sum 100 decimal digits per nonsquare.

problems.title: Path Sum: Two Ways
problems.method: Run one-row right/down dynamic programming on the official matrix.

problems.title: Path Sum: Three Ways
problems.method: Process columns with downward and upward relaxation passes.

problems.title: Path Sum: Four Ways
problems.method: Run Dijkstra on the four-neighbour matrix graph using an O(V^2) minimum scan.

problems.title: Monopoly Odds
problems.method: Power-iterate the 30,720-state cyclic-deck Markov chain, tracking square, consecutive doubles and both deck indices. The explicit initial deck order is one possible shuffle; tests compare a second ordering.

problems.title: Counting Rectangles
problems.method: Compare exact triangular-number products and stop each dimension once monotonicity excludes an improvement.

problems.title: Cuboid Route
problems.method: Enumerate largest side and summed smaller sides; count valid splits when the unfolded route is an integer.

problems.title: Prime Power Triples
problems.method: Enumerate bounded prime fourth powers, cubes and squares, deduplicating sums in a bitset.

problems.title: Product-sum Numbers
problems.method: Enumerate nondecreasing factors up to product 2K, infer padding ones, and sum distinct minima.

problems.title: Roman Numerals
problems.method: Decode each official Roman numeral and compare its length with the greedy canonical token length.

problems.title: Cube Digit Pairs
problems.method: Enumerate unordered pairs of six-digit sets, extending 6/9 only for display tests.

problems.title: Right Triangles with Integer Coordinates
problems.method: Count primitive perpendicular steps at each grid point; add the three axis cases. Every endpoint remains within the 50 by 50 grid.

problems.title: Arithmetic Expressions
problems.method: Enumerate every pairwise reduction of four distinct decimal digits using reduced rational arithmetic. This covers every binary expression tree, operator choice and parenthesization.

problems.title: Almost Equilateral Triangles
problems.method: Enumerate the increasing Pell solutions x^2 - 3y^2 = 4 and transform them into almost-equilateral triangles. Stop once every possible perimeter exceeds one billion.

problems.title: Amicable Chains
problems.method: Sieve proper-divisor sums, then traverse the resulting finite functional graph. Traversal labels locate cycles and count every vertex at most once.

problems.title: Su Doku
problems.method: Solve all 50 official grids by minimum-candidate backtracking with row, column and box masks. Require exactly one solution per grid.

problems.title: Large Non-Mersenne Prime
problems.method: Compute 28433 times 2^7830457 plus one modulo 10^10 using exact modular repeated squaring.

problems.title: Anagramic Squares
problems.method: For every anagram pair, enumerate all squares of its length, derive the injective letter-to-digit map and test the mapped partner with an exact integer square root.

problems.title: Largest Exponential
problems.method: Compare exact rational intervals for exponent times log(base), using an atanh series with a proven remainder bound. Overlapping intervals fall back to full GMP integer exponentiation.

problems.title: Arranged Probability
problems.method: Generate positive solutions of t(t-1) = 2b(b-1) by the Pell recurrence, stopping at the first total above 10^12.

problems.title: Optimum Polynomial
problems.method: Build Newton forward-difference interpolants in exact integer arithmetic and sum each fit at its first disagreement with the degree-ten generating polynomial.

problems.title: Triangle Containment
problems.method: Test the signs of three exact cross products. Strictly matching signs identify origin-containing triangles; edge and degenerate cases are excluded.

problems.title: Special Subset Sums: Optimum
problems.method: Construct a feasible upper bound from the six-element optimum supplied in the statement, then exhaustively search every increasing positive seven-element set of smaller sum. Prune subset-sum collisions and necessary cardinality inequalities.

problems.title: Pandigital Fibonacci Ends
problems.method: Track the last nine Fibonacci digits modulo 10^9. For each pandigital tail, compute the full Fibonacci number with GMP and check its leading nine digits exactly.

problems.title: Special Subset Sums: Testing
problems.method: Check the sorted smallest-(k+1) versus largest-k inequalities and sort all subset sums to detect collisions for each of the 100 official sets.

problems.title: Special Subset Sums: Meta-testing
problems.method: Count equal-size partitions of each 2k-element selection, subtracting Catalan partitions whose ordering already settles the sum comparison.

problems.title: Minimal Network
problems.method: Parse and validate the symmetric connected 40-node network. Subtract a Prim minimum spanning tree from the total weight of its undirected edges.

problems.title: Diophantine Reciprocals I
problems.method: Use (x-n)(y-n)=n^2 and search nonincreasing exponent vectors on consecutive primes. A constructed feasible primorial supplies a proven finite upper bound.

problems.title: Darts
problems.method: Choose a labelled double finishing region and enumerate zero, one or two earlier labelled dart regions, with the first two darts treated as an unordered multiset.

problems.title: Diophantine Reciprocals II
problems.method: Use the divisor count of n^2 and exhaust all nonincreasing prime-exponent vectors below a constructed feasible primorial. Saturate divisor products only after they exceed the target.

problems.title: Primes with Runs
problems.method: For each repeated digit, enumerate all choices of replacement positions and different digits, beginning with zero replacements. The first level producing primes determines the maximum repetition count.

problems.title: Bouncy Numbers
problems.method: Scan digit order and count numbers containing both a rise and a fall. Test the exact 99 percent proportion by integer cross multiplication.

problems.title: Non-bouncy Numbers
problems.method: Digit dynamic programming counts increasing and decreasing numbers at each length from one to 100. Subtract the nine constant-digit numbers counted twice at each length.

problems.title: Counting Block Combinations I
problems.method: Dynamic programming partitions rows by an initial black square or a red run of length at least three, followed by its required separator.

problems.title: Counting Block Combinations II
problems.method: Apply the separated-red-run recurrence with minimum length 50 until the count exceeds one million. Counts saturate above the threshold; twenty 51-cell blocks prove a finite bound.

problems.title: Red, Green or Blue Tiles
problems.method: For each tile length 2, 3 and 4, count tilings with black unit tiles and that colour alone, subtract the all-black row, then add the three counts.

problems.title: Red, Green, and Blue Tiles
problems.method: Count compositions of a 50-cell row by appending one of the allowed tile lengths 1, 2, 3 and 4.

problems.title: Pandigital Prime Sets
problems.method: Count primes for every digit subset, then memoize partitions of the full digit mask. Requiring the next block to contain the lowest remaining digit removes order duplicates.

problems.title: Digit Power Sum
problems.method: For an increasing decimal cutoff 10^d, enumerate powers of every possible digit sum 2 through 9d. Sort and deduplicate all matches; stop when the complete range contains 30 terms.

problems.title: Square Remainders
problems.method: Use the binomial remainder formula to obtain 2a floor((a-1)/2) for each a, then sum from 3 through 1000.

problems.title: Square Sum of the Digital Squares
Fractions and Sum of Powers of Two
Tours on a 4 \times N Playing Board
